subject: Confluo Labs — Integration flow validation and reference handshake
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@confluolabs.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@confluolabs.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Confluo Labs - integration validation: event webhook & batch fallback

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for taking this on. Attached is our current integration spec (confluo_integration_spec_v2.pdf) and a short reference payload. We want Redwood to validate two main flows before we move to an initial market test:

- Real-time event webhook handshake (JWT + ephemeral key rotation)
- Batch fallback processing for delayed payloads (>30s latency)

High level asks:
- Can your team run a reference validation in Redwood staging and confirm the auth flow and error-handling semantics?
- We'd like a short runbook and acceptance checklist so our implementation team can mirror it.
- Proposed window: Nov 9-10. Is that feasible?

Quick context: Confluo will send JSON payloads at variable QPS. The reference flow uses a signed header and expects a 202 vs 200 semantics for queued fallback. We flagged some failure modes in the spec.

Attachments: confluo_integration_spec_v2.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Director, Platform Partnerships
Confluo Labs
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@confluolabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Confluo Labs - integration validation: event webhook & batch fallback

Alyssa — thanks for the brief and the spec. We can take the Nov 9-10 window. Summary of what we'll deliver:

1) Staging validation run that exercises the JWT rotation handshake and the batch fallback path.
2) A short runbook with acceptance criteria and expected HTTP semantics (202 vs 200), retry hints, and logs to inspect.
3) A small CSV of test sequences that you can replay against our staging endpoint.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Please share staging creds and a sample production-ish payload set (or permission to synthesize).
- Confirm which fields in the payload Confluo considers authoritative for dedup keys.

Plan and owners:
- Sergio: validation orchestration, runbook draft, final signoff
- Marissa: test harness and load shaping, will provide sequence_test_template.csv
- Karthik: auth path and kernel-level timeouts, will validate token rotation behavior
- Laura: sandbox access and route provisioning

I'll attach the sequence_test_template.csv; Marissa will fill it with timings and edge cases. We will do an initial smoke run on Nov 9 morning and a deeper pass Nov 10.

Attachments: sequence_test_template.csv (csv)

Thanks,
Sergio
Director, Alliances
Redwood Inference

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa@confluolabs.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T08:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Confluo Labs - integration validation: event webhook & batch fallback

Looping in the implementation owners and giving a quick orchestration breakdown so the Confluo team knows what to expect. This will be a reply-all so Alyssa sees the tasking.

Orchestration checklist (short):
- Stage provisioning: Laura to create a route and ephemeral keyspace by 9:00 AM Nov 9
- Smoke test: Marissa to run 50 synthetic events (happy path) and 10 delayed events to validate the batch fallback queueing
- Auth validation: Karthik to run token rotation 3x and assert no dropped requests during rotation window
- Logging/observability: Sergio to provide the acceptance checklist plus log locations and sample queries

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- Webhook handshake returns 200 for inline processing, 202 for queued fallback within 5s of the delay threshold
- No duplicate dedup keys for the same payload across retry windows
- TTL-based KV eviction does not remove entries before 60s in the fallback queue

I'll kick off the smoke script at 9:15 AM PST and post the CSV results. If we hit auth flakes we'll pause and run a focused token rotation diagnostic.

Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Nov 8, 2026 at 11:30 AM Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com> wrote:

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@confluolabs.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@confluolabs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Confluo Labs - integration validation: event webhook & batch fallback

Sergio / team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Summary from our side after the two-day validation:

- Smoke pass: basic webhook handshake and inline processing passed (see attached sequence_test_results.csv).
- Failure observed: intermittent 401 during token rotation under burst conditions. We captured the logs and attached a short trace.
- Batch fallback: queued processing behavior and 202 semantics validated. TTL behavior observed matched expectations after we increased the queue TTL to 75s per your recommendation.

Next steps we propose:
1) Joint architecture walkthrough focused on token rotation edge cases and retry window behavior. Can the Redwood product engineer join on Nov 16 at 10:00 AM PST?
2) We'll sign an addendum to the SOW to include the extended auth SLA once we have the walkthrough notes. I will send the DocuSign link after the call.

Attachments: sequence_test_results.csv (csv)

Thanks again — great collaboration.

Best,
Alyssa Chen
Director, Platform Partnerships
Confluo Labs
